strategy.summary: Reproduce scipy#24558: scipy.linalg.sqrtm on singular nilpotent inputs returns huge finite values (~2.49e+291) instead of inf and emits no LinAlgWarning. The developer test test_gh24508 (parametrized over float32, float64, complex64, complex128) must fail on the buggy commit dd01e7df62f0 and pass on the fixed revision. Environment: Python 3.12, numpy 2.3.3, scipy 1.16.3 as reported in issue #24508, OpenBLAS 0.3.30, gcc 11.2 with gfortran; build from source is required because the fix lives in C sources (_matfuncs_sqrtm.c and _common_array_utils.h).

pinned_because: numpy 2.3.3 and scipy 1.16.3 are the versions reported in issue #24508; these are reported observations, not documented constraints
pybind11 2.13.6, cython 3.1.4, pythran 0.18.0 come from the issue's show_config build dependencies; numerically irrelevant, era-inferred only
OpenBLAS 0.3.30 from show_config; the LAPACK ?trsyl/dlanv2 path is where the garbage values originate

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/linalg/tests/test_matfuncs.py::TestSqrtm::test_gh24508 (parametrized dtyp in float32, float64, complex64, complex128)
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy dd01e7df62f0 the test fails: sqrtm returns finite values (~2.49e+291) in res[0,1:] so np.isinf is false, and/or pytest.warns(LinAlgWarning, match='Matrix is singular.') fails because no warning is raised. On the fixed revision the test passes: a LinAlgWarning with the message 'Matrix is singular.' is emitted and res[0,1:] are all inf, for all four dtypes.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import numpy as np, scipy.linalg as sl, warnings; warnings.simplefilter('always'); print(sl.sqrtm(np.array([[0,2,2],[0,0,0],[0,0,0]],dtype=np.float64)))"

input_output_examples.expected_output: upper-right entries are inf, with a LinAlgWarning raised
the same array with a LinAlgWarning: Matrix is singular. The result might be inaccurate or the array might not have a square root.

risks: The failure is a wrong-value / missing-warning defect, so the transition depends on the warning being absent on buggy code; the test's pytest.warns will fail there for the right reason only if the warning path is not triggered by other code.

The n==3 Sylvester 1x2/2x1 branch in the C code is the only path the evidence covers; the test does not exercise other sizes, and no tolerance is stated, so the check is inf and warning, not closeness.

The 2.49e+291 value comes from LAPACK ?trsyl and dlanv2 behaviour; the issue author suspects dlanv2 does not return 0.0. Whether garbage appears depends on OpenBLAS/LAPACK build and on isSchur reading out of bounds, which relies on platform memory zeroing. A reference LAPACK or a different OpenBLAS build may not reproduce the large value even on the buggy commit, and an ASan/valgrind build would expose the undefined read instead.

Two dependency versions (numpy 2.3.3, scipy 1.16.3) are reported observations from the issue, not documented constraints; the build is against the buggy commit's own source, so the scipy version is determined by the checkout rather than pip. Using a different numpy ABI with the buggy build may change behaviour.

The test is parametrized over float32 and complex64; single precision trsyl paths (strsyl/ctrsyl) may behave differently from double, so a pass on float64 does not prove the single-precision branches transition.
The C fix is in shared array utilities, so an incremental rebuild may be needed after switching between buggy and fixed revisions; stale build artifacts could make both runs look the same.

oracle.reference_source: the developer test assertions: pytest.warns(LinAlgWarning, match='Matrix is singular.') and np.isinf(res[0,1:]).all()
oracle.why: The developer test checks explicit inf entries and a warning rather than closeness, so no numeric tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On dd01e7df62f0, sqrtm returns finite values of about 2.49e+291 in res[0,1:] and emits no LinAlgWarning. np.isinf(res[0,1:]).all() is False and pytest.warns fails with no warning recorded, so the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision, sqrtm sets INFINITY for the zero-diagonal Sylvester case and emits LinAlgWarning 'Matrix is singular...'. np.isinf holds for res[0,1:] and pytest.warns matches, for all four dtypes.
